crm_notes:
High priority EU/UK enterprise account focused on low-latency regional search for regulated customers. Primary ask: handle ~300-500M indexed docs (mixed structured + attachments) with median query latency <= 120ms at 95th percentile for the top-10 pipeline (embedding search + neural reranker). Very cost-conscious — wants clear cost-per-query model and knob to trade accuracy vs unit cost.

POC scope: ingest 35M doc corpus subset first (legal precedents + client contracts), run two-week throughput and P95 latency tests. Evaluate two reranker modes: (1) local quantized reranker on dedicated nodes (faster, cheaper), (2) hosted larger reranker with regional failover. Wants fallback policy: if dedicated capacity saturated, route to smaller quantized model in the other EU region; also must support UK residency for certain clients (data segmentation).

Security/Compliance: must support SSO (SAML + SCIM), enterprise KMS integration, immutable audit logs for index mutations, 7/13/30/365 day retention options per dataset. Legal insisted on explicit data residency for telemetry/logs — not just model data.

Quote from CTO on 2026-02-18 call: "We need predictable worst-case latency — if 95th spikes we fail the feature. Also want linear cost estimates for scale; show us math for 500M docs."

Sales notes: AE introduced during GS session 2025-11-10. Initial interest came from internal search reliability pain after migration off legacy Solr cluster. Team has prior experience with Elastic + custom reranker but seeking unified platform with predictable unit economics and built-in failover.

What they like about Redwood: unified runtime across private/dedicated, transparent perf profiles, Optimize suggestions for batching/quant profiles. Concern: need contract language for UK-only residency and audit of telemetry paths.

Short bullets (shorthand, CRM-style):
- POC checklist in Drive: ingestion scripts, mapping, eval prompts
- Wants per-route dashboards + token-level cost breakdown
- Can do live demo week of 2026-03-15 (tentative)
- Need SE to run index throughput baseline (ingest 35M/day target)
- Legal will push back on any cross-border crash telemetry
